reasoning_content:
The GitHub release for RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z exists, and has an asset called minio.linux-amd64.RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z (need to verify). If I download the minio binary from GitHub, and mc likewise from the GitHub release of minio/mc, I can build an equivalent Docker image and tag it as minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z and minio/mc:RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z.

Let me verify the exact asset names:
- minio/minio release: `minio.linux-amd64.RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z`
- minio/mc release: RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z → `mc.linux-amd64.RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z`

Wait a sec — is the mc release tag for that exact version "RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z"? The minio/mc release uses the same naming convention. Let me check the GitHub API for the mc release.

Next, build the image:
- minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z: base is scratch/alpine, with the minio binary at /usr/bin/minio. The official image runs as the minio user and does `server /data --console-address ":9001"`. The healthcheck uses `curl -f http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live` — so curl needs to exist inside the image! Does the official minio image include a shell and curl? The official minio/minio image is based on... The healthcheck in the compose file uses `["CMD", "curl", "-f", ...]` — which means curl must exist in the official image (or else the healthcheck would always fail... in which case `condition: service_healthy` would never become true!). So the official image does include curl. I'll build an alpine-based image with the minio binary + curl installed.
- minio/mc:RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z: the createbuckets entrypoint uses `/bin/sh -c '...'` — the official mc image is based on busybox/alpine with sh. Build an alpine image with the mc binary at /usr/local/bin/mc.

After that, tag locally: docker build -t minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z, and similarly for mc. The compose `image:` specification will use the local tag without pulling... in practice, if `image:` is specified and the tag exists locally, compose won't pull.

This is a reasonable workaround for when the pinned image isn't obtainable from Docker Hub. Alternative: apt-get install minio? Not in Ubuntu 22.04's repositories. There's a minio package in the Debian repos, but... Ubuntu 22.04 doesn't have it. So building from the official GitHub binary is the best option.
